title: MoE-OPU: An FPGA Overlay Processor Leveraging Expert Parallelism for MoE-based Large Language Models
problem: MoE-based LLM inference on edge devices faces severe token allocation imbalances among experts, causing storage and computational burdens; lack of integration between expert-aware pruning and parallel scheduling leads to suboptimal resource utilization.
motivation: Enable scalable MoE-LLM inference on resource-constrained FPGA devices for edge deployment.
method: The processor speeds up MoE inference on an FPGA using three coordinated techniques. First, it removes unimportant weights from experts based on how often each expert gets used (keeping 25–75% depending on the usage pattern, expressed as ratios like 1:4 to 8:8), and stores numbers in space-saving formats (16-bit, 8-bit, or 4-bit precision). Second, it predicts which experts the next layer will need with an 83.4% success rate, so the hardware can load them in advance. Third, it uses a reconfigurable grid of processing cores (a systolic array) that can efficiently compute with both sparse weights and mixed-precision numbers in parallel.
key_novelty: It predicts which experts to use next and removes weights from rarely-used experts, both strategies guided by expert activation patterns, so prediction and pruning work as one system.
contributions: Activation-frequency-guided N:M sparsity and mixed-precision quantization
Lightweight prediction network for proactive expert scheduling
Reconfigurable systolic array architecture for efficient MoE computation

metrics.speedup: 6.78× vs NVIDIA A100, 13.37× vs RTX 4090, 7.85× vs Xilinx U200 FPGA

limitations: Specific to MoE architectures; may not generalize to other sparse model types.
